meta.why: Topics this fleet does not write about AT ALL — not carefully, not hedged, not with a disclaimer. Distinct from HEALTH_CLAIM_RE in checks.mjs, which only catches a curative CLAIM ('cures cancer'). A thread can be immaculately hedged and still be a cancer thread; this table blocks the TOPIC, whatever the wording.
meta.operator: 2026-08-21 — 'Avoid any topic that is cancer-related. We do not write about cancer treatment or anything.' Then 2026-09-29 — 'We should fix the rule to block it if cancer is the main focus of the post. If it's an idea inside a body then it should be fine. We avoid making claims about curing cancers or any shit like that.'
meta.modes: A topic is 'always' by default: any term anywhere blocks the thread. A topic with "mode": "focus" blocks only when it is the post's SUBJECT: a `terms` word in the hook, or in at least max(focus.minTweets, focus.minShare of the tweets) tweets. Its `alwaysTerms` and `phrases` (treatment and patient-journey wording) still block anywhere, and "claims": true blocks any sentence that pairs a term with a claim to treat, cure, prevent, shrink, fight or lower the risk of it, wherever it sits. A string is read as a hook; a list is read as a thread, index 0 being the hook.
meta.enforcement: bannedTopicIssue() in checks.mjs. Hard error at generation (validateDraft), at QC (checkThread), in the hand lane (validate-thread.mjs), and at donor selection so a banned donor never enters the pool in the first place.
meta.addingATopic: Add a block below. Keep terms lowercase; they are matched case-insensitively on word boundaries. Prefer a term that is unambiguous on its own over a broad one that needs context — a false block costs one thread, a false pass costs the account.

topics.label: cancer and oncology
topics.why: Supplement content adjacent to cancer is the highest-liability copy we could write: it reaches people making treatment decisions, it is what platform health policies and the FTC police hardest, and no commission is worth implying a supplement bears on a cancer outcome. The ban is on the SUBJECT, so 'what I'd do if I had cancer' is blocked even though it claims nothing. Since 2026-09-29 that means the SUBJECT is cancer (the hook, or a thread that keeps returning to it): a passing mention inside a body is allowed, and any claim to treat, cure, prevent or lower the risk of it is blocked wherever it sits.
